liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (5 reviews): First Dark Star in a first set since 1971; it doesn't go far; Dark Star appears in the first set, which the reviewer finds striking [13][17][20][21][22]
- **Victim Or The Crime** (3 reviews): Bruce leads the band from Scarlet into Victim and back out to Fire, with strong interplay with Jerry; Bruce totally leads the band into Victim in the Scarlet > Victim > Fire sequence [11][17][22]
- **Standing On the Moon** (2 reviews): The reprise slows down into a perfect Standing On the Moon; Standing On the Moon is the only song played to 1991 standard, per this reviewer [18][21]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Bruce's runs in the Jack Straw and Bertha openers are stunning [12]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Bruce riffs over everything and begins steering toward Victim about five and a half minutes into Scarlet [12]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin' has a long exploratory jam leading into the drums [13]
- **Playin' In The Band Reprise** (1 review): The jam coming out of space bubbles up into a sweet Playin' reprise [18]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Good Lovin' closes the set; Jerry sings 'Doctor, Doctor' so hard the reviewer feared he'd blow a gasket [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-08-16.sbd.nickc.111330.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 211 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd91-08-16.sbd.braverman.6676.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 172 min; rated 4.25/5 by 32 [3]. Said about its sound: Phil's bass strings sound loose during the first set, giving an odd but appealing tone; Phil's bass has an odd problem during Jack Straw, which the reviewer finds novel; Reviewer calls the sound muddy and the playing sloppy by 1991 standards [12][16][21][22]
- **gd91-08-16.sbd.17011.sbeok.flac**: soundboard; 18 songs; 158 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1991-08-16.141274.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 17 songs; 161 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]

## Around the show

- The Dark Star was supposedly played for poster artist Rick Griffin, hospitalized after a motorcycle accident [13]
- Reviewer recalls Bruce Hornsby saying the Dead's biggest problem was inconsistency [16]
- Reviewer finds it far more smokin' than the average 1991 show [16]
- Reviewer ranks this among the three best shows of 1991, crediting Hornsby with pushing Jerry [19]
- Reviewer doubts it is a top-three show of 1991; well played but short on energy for that lineup [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-08-16.sbd.nickc.111330.flac16**: transferred by nickc; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Uploader credits Nick for many DAT masters and clones, recorded with the uploader's own mics and gear; Admin note: the source was first called an audience master, then corrected to a soundboard [1]
- **gd91-08-16.sbd.braverman.6676.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD:DAT> DAT> SF> WAV> SHN [3]
- **gd91-08-16.sbd.17011.sbeok.flac**: source: SB DAT 48khz low-gen clone [2]
- **gd1991-08-16.141274.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Wolfgang's: [Grateful Dead Laminate from Shoreline Amphitheatre, Aug 16, 1991 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/backstage-passes/grateful-dead/laminate/SHO910816.html) [24]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1991-08-16 Grateful Dead Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1991-08-16-grateful-dead-ticket/) [25]
